Use this opening paragraph to state the practical question in plain language. Keep it short: what problem does the note address, who is it for, and why does it matter?

## Main Point

State the core idea in one or two paragraphs. This section should be readable on its own for someone scanning the page.

:::: {.index-list}
::: {.index-item}
### Key Takeaway

Summarize the most important observation, method choice, or recommendation.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Why It Matters

Explain the practical consequence for reporting, analysis, data collection, or decision-making.
:::
::::

## Context

Describe the source material, workflow, or reporting situation at a high level. Avoid publishing private report contents or raw client data. Good public-safe context includes the type of source, the kind of workflow, the question being asked, and the limitations that affect interpretation.

## Method Notes

Use this section to document how the analysis or workflow was handled.

:::: {.index-list}
::: {.index-item}
### Inputs

List the kinds of inputs involved, such as platform exports, spreadsheets, transcripts, surveys, scraped public sources, or report artifacts.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Processing Steps

Describe the cleaning, classification, coding, validation, or reporting steps at a level that helps readers trust the process.
:::

::: {.index-item}
### Limitations

Name what the data or method cannot answer, any assumptions made, and what should be reviewed before using the findings.
:::
::::

## Example Structure

```{=html}
<div class="card-grid">
  <article class="content-card">
    <h3>Finding</h3>
    <p>Use this card for a concise finding, pattern, or comparison.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="content-card">
    <h3>Evidence</h3>
    <p>Use this card to describe the source of evidence without exposing private details.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="content-card">
    <h3>Decision Use</h3>
    <p>Use this card to explain how the insight could support a practical next step.</p>
  </article>
</div>
```

## What To Do With This

Close with the practical takeaway: what the reader should define, check, build, review, or decide next.
